title: Best local LLM setup suggestions
author: pasqui23
selftext:
I hate subscriptions and could not afford them after buying my Ryzen Max 395 with 128GB of RAM.

 What workflow would you suggest, especially since I am working with godot?

comments.author: sunnystormy64
comments.body: Any models that are GSQ RCO quantized on HuggingFace are fair game. Look for image-text-to-text reasoning models that have published benchmarks on their model card and try getting them up and running on your machine. I know that you are averse to subscriptions, but OpenCode offers free cloud model usage with open-weight models for a limited time per day. I've purchased their Go subscription for $40/month and have NEVER run out of usage with MiMo v2.6 Pro orchestrating everything. So, TLDR, get a cloud model to setup your local reasoning model and see if it works for you.

comments.author: WhosLive
comments.body: With 128GB unified memory you can run fairly big models, so a coding-focused open-weight model through Ollama or LM Studio, hooked into an editor agent like Cline, Continue or OpenCode, is usually the easiest local setup for Godot. For AGENTS.md, a short file works best: engine version (Godot 4.x, GDScript), project folder layout, naming and signal conventions, and a rule to run the project or tests after each change. Local models tend to do better with small, specific tasks than big refactors, so keeping scenes and scripts small helps a lot. MCP servers that let the agent read Godot's docs or run the project and return errors are worth a look, and keep the comfyui side separate for art.
